cards.explanation: The answer is the sand of the sea, friends. Go ahead and try counting that at the beach. You'll quit around grain number forty and just enjoy the view. The verse says the number of the Israelites cannot be measured or counted (Hosea 1:10), and it comes right after all those hard words about "…not My people…"

The answer is sons of the living God. Hear that slowly, friends. In the very place where it was said, "You are not My people…" that's the new name they'll be called (Hosea 1:10). Same spot, brand new label.

The answer is Judah. The verse says the people of Judah and of Israel will be gathered together (Hosea 1:11). Two groups who were apart end up in one place. I think that's good news for anybody who's ever had a group chat go quiet.
The answer is False. The text says they will appoint for themselves one leader (Hosea 1:11). Not a committee, not a panel, just one. Picture a kitchen with one head baker. Things go smoother.
The answer is "My people." That's what the LORD says to call the brothers (Hosea 2:1). Back in Hosea 1:9 the words were "…not My people…" Now the words are flipped around.

The answer is True. The LORD says to say of your sisters, "My loved one." Brothers get "My people" and sisters get "My loved one," and both names come in the same verse (Hosea 2:1). I think that's a lot of warmth packed into one line.

The answer is her adultery and unfaithfulness, friends. The LORD says she is not His wife and He is not her husband, and He wants her to remove the adultery and the unfaithfulness (Hosea 2:2). It's a hard verse, but the way out is right there in it.

The answer is thirst. The LORD says He'll make her like a desert and a parched land, and let her die of thirst (Hosea 2:3). I think this is a heavy one, so let's just take it seriously. The picture is of a dry, empty place with nothing to drink.

The answer is False, and that's what the text says. The LORD says, "I will have no compassion on her children, because they are the children of adultery" (Hosea 2:4). The reason is in the verse itself. I think it's one of the heavy lines of this chapter.

The answer is food and clothes, friends. She thought, "I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and water, wool and linen, oil and drink" (Hosea 2:5). Bread, water, oil and drink are the food side, and wool and linen are the clothes. Notice it's what she thought. The next verses talk about what the LORD says He gave her.

The answer is so she can't find her way. He says He'll hedge up her path with thorns and enclose her with a wall, "…so she cannot find her way" (Hosea 2:6). Hedged with thorns, enclosed with a wall. That's a lot standing in her way.

The answer is False. She will pursue her lovers but not catch them, and she will seek them but not find them (Hosea 2:7). Two verbs of chasing and two of coming up empty. It's like sprinting for the elevator and watching the doors close.

The answer is husband. The verse says she will say, "I will return to my first husband…" (Hosea 2:7). That's a turn in her thinking, once she can't catch her lovers. It's the first time in this part that she talks about returning instead of chasing.

The answer is the LORD. He says it was He who gave her grain, new wine and oil, and who lavished on her silver and gold (Hosea 2:8). She does not acknowledge it. Not acknowledging who baked the cookies is awkward at any table.

The answer is take them back, friends. The LORD says, "…I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season…" (Hosea 2:9). Notice He calls them "My" grain and "My" new wine. The gifts were His to begin with.

The answer is True. The LORD says the wool and linen "…were given to cover her nakedness" (Hosea 2:9). They were gifts with a purpose, and He's the one who gave them. When He says He'll take them away, that's the weight of it.

The answer is False. The LORD says He will expose her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of His hands (Hosea 2:10). Her lovers can't rescue her. I think that's the hard truth under all these lines.

The answer is her feasts and Sabbaths, friends. The LORD says He will put an end to all her exultation: her feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths, all her appointed feasts (Hosea 2:11). That's the whole calendar of celebrations. The list in the verse is long, so it's good to catch the right part.

The answer is a thicket. The LORD says He'll destroy her vines and fig trees and make them into a thicket, and the beasts of the field will devour them (Hosea 2:12). Vines and fig trees turned into a thicket is a heavy picture. I think this is one of the hard lines in this chapter.

The answer is forgot. The LORD ends the list with, "But Me she forgot…" declares the LORD (Hosea 2:13). After all the rings, jewelry and incense, that's the line that sums it up. It's the heart of the whole speech.
